heading: INT. ELEVATOR HOISTWAY, OFFICE TOWER - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ELEVATOR HOISTWAY, OFFICE TOWER - NIGHT
A concrete shaft lit by a single work lamp.
Greasy cables hang in the dark.
Far below, a pit.
Far above, a rectangle of light.
ISAAC MBEKI, thirties, an elevator mechanic, clings to a ladder bolted to the wall.
He wears a headlamp and a harness that does not look new.
A radio crackles at his hip.
He glances up.
A set of boots has appeared in the light above him.
CELESTE ARNAUD, forties, in a good coat, stands on the landing with a pistol held low.
She has the posture of a woman who has done this before.
She does not speak.
His breath catches.
He takes a step down the ladder.
She takes one down after him.
The cable between them hums.
Isaac, you there? Control room. We've lost the car on four.
units.name: RADIO

units.text: He keeps his eyes on her and unclips the radio.
Say again.
units.name: ISAAC

units.text: Car's stuck between four and five. Don't move the cab.
units.name: RADIO

units.text: She raises the pistol a few inches.
He hears the safety click.
Copy. Hold the car. I'm coming up.
units.name: ISAAC

units.text: Who are you talking to?
units.name: RADIO

units.text: He does not answer.
He drops the radio.
It falls forty feet, bouncing off the guide rails, then shatters on the pit floor.
She fires.
The round whines off a rail.
He kicks away from the ladder, swings on the cable, and lets go.
A moving counterweight rises out of the dark and he lands on it hard, flat, wind knocked from him.
She leans over the edge, searching the black.
The counterweight sinks.
Her face shrinks in the rectangle of light.
He lies there, shaking, laughing silently, and does not move for a very long time.
